messages:
ashley: heads-up — we're still seeing a nontrivial tail of clients sending the old RPC envelope wrapper. breaks a few v3 assumptions (plain json body + typed headers).

ben: do we have numbers? rough % or top-ten tenants?

ashley: ~2.7% overall last 24h, skewed to two older tenants and a bunch of mobile sdk versions. top tenant sent ~11k/day. logged to legacy_envelope.count.

kai: oof. we said we'd deprecate, but we also promised no hard breaks. options: 1) server-side adapter that strips envelope, 2) require client opt-in via header + fallback, 3) longer deprecation with telemetry-only.

ashley: leaning toward a minimal runtime adapter (an "envelope-stripper") behind a feature flag so we can measure perf + cost. runtime should decode/envelope->body only when header `X-RW-Envelope: 1` or content-type `application/rpc-envelope` present. otherwise no CPU hit.

samir: important: make it tenant-configurable in Private/Dedicated so security teams can opt-out. also add size limit and reject if envelope > 1MB.

ashley: agreed. design notes:
- default: disabled for new tenants
- enable per-tenant opt-in via console toggle `compat.envelope_strip`
- rollout plan: canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4 weeks, with fast rollback if latency > +10ms p50 or error rate increase > 0.5%

ben: what about telemetry and notices to users? we should return a deprecation warning header when we accept an envelope so clients see it: `X-RW-Deprecated: envelope; until=2027-09-01`. also emit `legacy_envelope.accepted` with tenant tag.

kai: add guardrails: a) rate-limit decoding to avoid bursty CPU, b) run path profiling so hot paths unaffected, c) static decode pool to avoid GC churn.

ashley: implementation plan: small middleware in runtime (C++ path) to detect header/content-type and call into existing decoder (reuse code from on-prem shim). keep logic tiny — decode, validate schema v3, replace body, and attach `x-rw-compat: envelope-stripped` header.

lina: do we need an API-level-by-default fallback for hosted API? i.e. accept older auth tokens + envelope? or keep auth checks identical after decode?

ashley: do auth after decode. preserves security model. but we'll add telemetry to flag any auth anomalies (legacy_envelope.auth_fail).

deploy-bot: staging-deploy started for branch: feature/envelope-stripper (sha: ab12c3d)

ben: testing: add e2e matrix for envelope true/false, content sizes (small/large), and malformed payloads. also simulate heavy concurrent envelope traffic to validate CPU safety.

samir: ops note — cost impact: decode CPU + memory; we should bind cost to tenant so customers enabling compat pay marginally for decode ops (billing tag `compat.decode_cpu`).

ashley: rollout docs: console will show per-tenant toggle, rollout progress, and a table of top callers still sending envelope. will email top two tenants with migration guidance and example code to remove envelope.

kai: lifecycle: keep the adapter for 6 months after GA, then warn for 60 days and remove. exact dates in RFC follow-up. also make the console show deprecation calendar so tenants can plan.

ben: I'll file the follow-up RFC with attachments: mini-arch diagram, perf microbench, telemetry plan, and the removal timeline. assign to @kai + @samir for review.

ashley: thanks — if no objections by EOD we'll canary next week.

lina: +1 from security, provided auth-after-decode and size cap.

kai: +1 from runtime — will drop perf numbers in RFC.

ben: assigning action items:
- ben: write RFC + rollout playbook
- kai: perf microbench + static pool prototype
- samir: console toggle + billing tag plan
- ashley: tenant outreach draft

ashley: cool. ping me when RFC is up.

ben: RFC PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pulls/482 — review pls :)
